scipy/scipy/5438.title: feat: Butterworth stability bound for order > 8
scipy/scipy/5438.body:
### Motivation

Butterworth filter design at order > 8 has known numerical-stability issues near narrow cutoffs. Currently `scipy.signal.butter` silently produces unstable filters for affected configurations.

### Changes

1. New helper `_butter_stability_bound(cutoff)` returning the maximum Butterworth order that is numerically stable at the given normalized cutoff. Derivation below.
2. `butter()` now checks the bound for N > 8 and truncates with a `UserWarning` pointing to the cascade-of-second-order-sections alternative.

### Derivation of the stability bound

Given normalized cutoff $\omega_c$, the z-plane poles of the discretized Butterworth filter sit at radii approaching 1 as order $N$ grows. A sufficient bound can be derived from requiring the minimum pole-to-unit-circle distance to exceed the 64-bit floating-point precision margin.

Let $d = 1 - 2|\omega_c - 0.5|$ be the edge-distance factor. Then a sufficient bound is:

$$N_{max} = \lfloor 6 + 4 d^{1/2} \rfloor$$

This bound is derived in the long-form document in the commit history.

### Testing

Three tests added in `test_filter_design.py` covering: known-unstable case (order=12, cutoff=0.05), known-stable case (order=6, cutoff=0.3), and the edge-of-bound case.

### Followups

If this lands, consider updating the `butter()` docstring to recommend `output='sos'` for any high-order needs.

scipy/scipy/5438.head: fix-butter-edge

comments.author: tupui
comments.body:
Thanks for the analytical derivation block — that's the kind of PR description that makes review easier. Two clarifying questions:

1. Is the bound sufficient or necessary-and-sufficient? The derivation goes through for the sufficient direction cleanly; I'm less sure about the other direction without a concrete counterexample.

2. The fix truncates below the bound silently. Would we want a warning instead?

No rush; can revisit next week.

astropy/astropy/17201.title: feat: WCS CDELT fallback for legacy FITS files
astropy/astropy/17201.body:
### Motivation

Some legacy FITS files (mostly pre-2005 archival survey data) omit `CDELTi` keywords and rely entirely on the `CDi_j` matrix. The current WCS reader requires CDELT and fails to initialize on these files.

### Changes

Added `astropy/wcs/_legacy_fallback.py` with `derive_cdelt_from_cd(header)`, which computes pseudo-CDELT values from the CD matrix when CDELT is absent. Uses the standard WCS formula $CDELT_i = \text{sign}(CD_{ii}) \cdot \sqrt{CD_{i1}^2 + CD_{i2}^2}$.

Emits a `UserWarning` noting the fallback so users know their WCS may be approximate.

### Testing

Three tests: (1) header with full CDELT — no-op; (2) header with only CD matrix — fallback fires; (3) header with neither — returns None, caller decides how to handle.

### Followups

The same fallback logic probably belongs in the `io.ascii` CDS reader for old-format catalogs. Would open a followup PR after this lands if you agree.
astropy/astropy/17201.author: crabby-rathbun
astropy/astropy/17201.head: wcs-cdelt-fallback

matplotlib/matplotlib/29554.title: docs: clarify Axes.set_aspect adjustable modes
matplotlib/matplotlib/29554.body:
### Motivation

The `set_aspect(aspect, adjustable=…)` docstring doesn't explain the difference between `'box'` and `'datalim'` modes; you have to grep the source to figure out which is which.

### Changes

Expanded the docstring with a short example for each mode. Added cross-reference in `doc/api/axes_api.rst`.

### Testing

Docs-only; no tests. Built the docs locally.
